metadata.title: Cook's Exit, Apple's New AI Power Map, and the Privacy Balance | WWDC26

conclusion: At WWDC26 Tim Cook hosts his last keynote to a near-minute ovation as John Ternus prepares to become CEO in September. The episode asks if post-Cook Apple can define consumer AI again. After Apple Intelligence's 2024 stumble and 2025 delivery crisis, it maps the power reset — Cook intervening, Rockwell owning Siri under Federighi, Gemini veteran Amar Subramanya on models, Giannandrea exiting — plus Private Cloud Compute on Google Cloud TEEs and App Intents as the agentic bridge. Wall Street loved Cook's 15 years; Ternus must prove product.
background: Silicon Valley 101 reports from WWDC26 after two years of Apple AI disappointment: delayed features, lawsuits over advertised capabilities, and a 2025 'AI crisis' for a company wired for yearly big-bang releases that look glacial versus model cadence. Guests contrast Apple's distribution moat with the lack of a SOTA foundation model, and unpack why PCC on Google Cloud is both a privacy bet and a hardware-trust engineering problem.
important_facts: 2024-06-10 Apple Intelligence was followed by slips; 2025 marketed undelivered AI and drew litigation. A secret early-2025 meeting chaired by then-COO Jeff Williams reframed failure as org/culture/leadership: John Giannandrea lost Cook's trust; Mike Rockwell (ex-Vision Pro) took Siri under Craig Federighi rather than becoming top AI chief; Amar Subramanya (16 years Google on Gemini/Bard, briefly Microsoft) joined as model lead; Giannandrea later left. Cook became hands-on on AI; Ternus inherits as CEO after September 2026.

WWDC demos emphasize agentic Siri via App Intents: developers declare structured actions/data so Siri can tool-call into apps. Guests say Apple is early — third-party depth thin, US-first rollout likely. Private Cloud Compute aims for stateless encrypted inference with no retention for training/profiling; new PCC stacks Google Cloud hardware with Intel TDX-style confidential VMs so Apple Silicon security ideas travel off-device.

Investor take: Cook's 15 years were a Wall Street honeymoon with fewer product fireworks; Ternus faces a 'return to product era.' Distribution and privacy remain assets; Gemini partnership plus Amar's hire buy time while Apple proves self-model competence.

mental_model.name: AI Power Map × Privacy Compute × Agentic Distribution
mental_model.components: Separate who owns AI inside Apple, how private-cloud TEEs extend on-device trust to Google Cloud, and how App Intents turn the installed base into an agent runtime. Judge Apple AI by shipping cadence and third-party tool depth.
mental_model.application: Long AAPL if Ternus shows faster AI delivery and real App Intents adoption; track GOOGL as competitor and PCC/Gemini partner. Privacy is a moat only if TEEs stay performant and regulators accept hybrid cloud.

key_insights.view: Apple's AI crisis was organizational before model-sized.
key_insights.question: Why reorganize?
key_insights.answer: Yearly perfect-experience culture failed against weekly model shifts; Rockwell/Federighi/Subramanya redraw ownership so Siri ships inside software while models get a Gemini-hardened lead.

key_insights.view: PCC on Google Cloud exports Apple trust to TEEs.
key_insights.question: Is privacy theater?
key_insights.answer: Design is stateless: encrypt, compute, wipe. Hard part is cost/perf of confidential inference at global scale.

key_insights.view: App Intents is the quiet agent strategy.
key_insights.question: Where is the iPhone moment?
key_insights.answer: When Siri reliably tool-calls third-party apps end-to-end. Distribution is the edge; unfinished developer surface is the gap.

top_investment_implications.thesis: Distribution + privacy + cash intact; Ternus must ship Siri utility from WWDC demos — medium, execution-sensitive
Gemini partner and PCC cloud substrate; Apple demand signals confidential compute — low confidence
Subramanya briefly stopped at Microsoft before Apple hire — talent-flow datapoint, not a core thesis

golden_quotes: Apple is the definer, not the follower.
